questions.text: Explain three different operational modes of dual-processor architecture used in Stored Program Control (SPC) electronic switching systems: (a) Standby mode, (b) Synchronous duplex mode, and (c) Load sharing mode. Discuss reliability and fault tolerance.

Explain the operation of Time-Space-Time (TST) and Space-Time-Space (STS) multi-stage digital switches with necessary block diagrams. Compare their blocking probabilities, implementation complexity, and cross-point requirements.

What is Common Channel Signaling (CCS)? Describe the SS7 protocol stack architecture (MTP Level 1-3, SCCP, TCAP, ISUP) with a neat block diagram and compare CCS with channel-associated in-band signaling.

Define Erlang, Grade of Service (GoS), and blocking probability in telephone traffic engineering. State Erlang-B formula: $B(c, A) = \frac{A^c / c!}{\sum_{k=0}^c A^k / k!}$. During busy hour, an average of $30\text{ Erlangs}$ is offered to a group of trunks; calculate carried traffic, lost traffic, and required number of lines for a given GoS.

Explain the operation of Circuit Switching, Message Switching, and Packet Switching (Virtual Circuit vs Datagram networks) with timing diagrams and compare them in terms of call setup delay, dedicated bandwidth, and latency.

What are the purposes and functions of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU)? Explain the regulatory and policy role of the Nepal Telecommunications Authority (NTA) in the development of the telecom sector in Nepal.

What is Softswitch and Next Generation Network (NGN)? Explain the functional separation of Call Control and Bearer Transport, Media Gateways (MG), and Media Gateway Controllers (MGC) using SIP and MEGACO protocols.
Explain National and International Numbering Plans according to ITU-T Recommendation E.164 (Country Code, National Destination Code, and Subscriber Number).

Compare guided transmission media used in telecommunication networks: Twisted Pair, Coaxial Cable, and Optical Fiber. Explain the propagation of light through optical fiber, acceptance angle, and single-mode versus multi-mode fiber characteristics.
What is Time Division Multiplexing (TDM)? How does Statistical TDM (STDM) overcome the limitations and bandwidth wastage of synchronous TDM? Explain STDM frame structure with address overhead.
Differentiate between Infinite Source (Lost Calls Cleared - Erlang B), Lost Calls Delayed (Erlang C queuing model), and Finite Source (Engset model) traffic systems in telecommunication networks.

What is ISDN? Explain the architectural reference model, reference points (R, S, T, U), functional devices (NT1, NT2, TE1, TE2, TA), and compare Basic Rate Interface ($2B+D$) and Primary Rate Interface ($30B+D$).
Explain Digital Subscriber Line (xDSL) architecture: compare ADSL, VDSL, and HDSL. Explain Discrete Multi-Tone (DMT) modulation, POTS splitters, and downstream/upstream frequency division.

Explain Routing and Congestion Control in packet switching networks: compare Distance Vector Routing (Bellman-Ford) with Link State Routing (Dijkstra), and explain Leaky Bucket and Token Bucket traffic shaping algorithms.
Explain Voice over IP (VoIP) network operation: Describe the roles of RTP/RTCP for media transport and SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) for session setup, modification, and termination.

Describe Stored Program Control (SPC) in digital telephone exchanges. Explain centralized vs distributed SPC architectures and detail the basic software call processing steps from off-hook to call teardown.

Derive Erlang's Lost Call Formula (Erlang-B formula) $B(c, A) = \frac{A^c / c!}{\sum_{k=0}^c A^k / k!}$ for a telephone trunk group of $c$ circuits with offered traffic load $A$ in Erlangs under Blocked Calls Cleared (BCC) assumptions. Calculate blocking probability for $c=4, A=2\text{ Erlangs}$.
questions.solutionOutline: Models telephone loss system with c servers and no waiting buffer. Markov chain state k represents k busy trunks. Transition rate up is lambda, transition rate down is k*mu. State probabilities follow truncated Poisson distribution P_k = (A^k / k!) / sum_{i=0}^c (A^i / i!). Blocking probability B is probability all c trunks are busy: B = P_c. For c=4, A=2: term 0: 1, term 1: 2, term 2: 2, term 3: 4/3, term 4: 2/3. Sum = 7. B = (2/3) / 7 = 2/21 approx 0.0952 (9.52%).

questions.text: Explain Erlang's Delay Formula (Erlang-C formula) for Blocked Calls Delayed (BCD) queuing systems. Derive average queue length, average waiting time in queue ($W_q$), and probability of delay exceeding $t$ seconds in call center switching systems.
questions.solutionOutline: Models M/M/c queuing system with infinite queue buffer. Arriving call finding all c trunks busy enters queue rather than being dropped. Erlang-C formula gives probability that arriving call experiences delay: P(>0) = [A^c / (c! (1 - A/c))] * P_0. Average waiting time for all calls W_q = P(>0) / [c mu (1 - A/c)]. Probability delay exceeds t is P(W > t) = P(>0) exp(-c mu (1 - A/c) t).

questions.text: Explain Space-Division Switching and Time-Division Switching. Derive the minimum number of crosspoints for a non-blocking 3-stage Clos Network $N_c = 2Nk + k(N/n)^2$, and state Clos's condition $k \ge 2n - 1$.
questions.solutionOutline: Crossbar switches require N^2 crosspoints. Multi-stage Clos network: N inputs partitioned into N/n input switches of size n x k; intermediate stage has k switches of size (N/n) x (N/n); output stage has N/n switches of size k x n. Strict non-blocking condition requires middle stage switches k >= 2n - 1 (in worst case, calling inlet has n-1 busy outlets and called outlet has n-1 busy inlets; requires 2n-1 paths). Minimizing with respect to n yields optimal crosspoints proportional to N^(1.5).

questions.text: Explain Time Slot Interchange (TSI) and Time-Multiplexed Space (TMS) switching modules. Contrast Time-Space-Time (TST) and Space-Time-Space (STS) multi-stage digital switches with complexity analysis.
questions.solutionOutline: TSI stores PCM samples in Speech Memory and reads out in different time slot order using Control Memory. TMS transfers samples between physical highways at same time slot. TST switch: first stage TSI shifts slot, middle stage TMS transfers highways, final stage TSI shifts to desired destination slot. STS switch: space stage selects highway, time stage shifts slot, output space routes to port. TST preferred for large digital exchanges because TSI memory is cheaper than high-speed space crosspoints.

questions.text: Describe Common Channel Signaling System No. 7 (SS7) architecture. Explain the four levels of the SS7 protocol stack (MTP-1, MTP-2, MTP-3, and SCCP/ISUP/TCAP) and signaling network nodes (SP, STP, SCP).
questions.solutionOutline: Out-of-band packet-switched signaling network for telecommunications. Levels: MTP-1 (physical 64 kbps link); MTP-2 (data link framing, error control, sequence numbering); MTP-3 (network routing, signaling traffic management); ISUP (ISDN User Part for call setup/teardown); SCCP (Signaling Connection Control Part for global title translation); TCAP (transaction capabilities for database queries like 800-numbers/roaming). Nodes: Service Switching Point (SSP), Signaling Transfer Point (STP), Service Control Point (SCP).

questions.text: Explain Channel-Associated Signaling (CAS) vs Common-Channel Signaling (CCS). Discuss why CCS replaced CAS in modern telecommunication networks with respect to trunk utilization, setup speed, and fraud prevention.
questions.solutionOutline: CAS carries signaling information inside same physical trunk/time-slot dedicated to voice call (e.g. in-band DTMF or TS16 multi-frame in E1). Inefficient, slow call setup, vulnerable to blue-box tone fraud. CCS separates all signaling onto dedicated packet-switched data network (SS7/SIGTRAN) serving thousands of voice trunks. Benefits: sub-second call setup, trunk optimization (trunks seized only upon call answer), advanced database services, and absolute immunity to in-band tone fraud.

questions.text: Describe the Plesiochronous Digital Hierarchy (PDH) and Synchronous Digital Hierarchy (SDH). Detail the E1 primary rate frame structure ($2.048\text{ Mbps}$, 32 time slots of $64\text{ kbps}$, frame alignment in TS0, signaling in TS16).
questions.solutionOutline: E1 standard: 8 kHz sampling rate (frame duration 125 us). 32 channels x 8 bits/channel = 256 bits/frame. Bit rate = 256 bits * 8000 frames/s = 2.048 Mbps. TS0 carries Frame Alignment Signal (FAS) and CRC-4 error checking. TS16 carries CAS signaling. TS1-TS15 and TS17-TS31 carry 30 digital voice/data channels. PDH multiplexes E1 to E2/E3/E4 using bit stuffing (demultiplexing requires cascading back down). SDH solves this via synchronous byte-interleaved mapping.

questions.text: Describe Synchronous Digital Hierarchy (SDH) and SONET frame structures. Explain STM-1 frame structure ($155.52\text{ Mbps}$, 9 rows $\times$ 270 columns), Section Overhead (SOH), Path Overhead (POH), and pointer justification mechanisms.
questions.solutionOutline: STM-1 frame has 9 rows x 270 columns of bytes transmitted every 125 us. Bit rate = 9 * 270 * 8 * 8000 = 155.52 Mbps. First 9 columns: Regenerator Section Overhead (RSOH, rows 1-3), Pointer row (row 4), Multiplex Section Overhead (MSOH, rows 5-9). Remaining 261 columns carry Virtual Container (VC-4 payload) with 1 column of Path Overhead (POH). AU-4 pointer indicates starting byte location of VC-4, accommodating phase/frequency jitter via positive/negative byte justification without slip buffers.

questions.text: Explain Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) and Dense WDM (DWDM). Describe optical transponders, optical add-drop multiplexers (OADM/ROADM), and Erbium-Doped Fiber Amplifiers (EDFA) in long-haul optical networks.
questions.solutionOutline: WDM multiplexes multiple independent optical carrier wavelengths on single optical fiber strand. Coarse WDM uses 20 nm channel spacing. DWDM uses ITU-T 100 GHz (0.8 nm) or 50 GHz (0.4 nm) spacing in C-band (1530-1565 nm), multiplexing 80+ channels to achieve terabit capacities. ROADM allows remote dynamic rerouting and insertion/extraction of wavelengths. EDFA amplifies all C-band wavelengths simultaneously using 980/1480 nm pump laser without electronic regeneration.

questions.text: Describe Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN). Compare Basic Rate Interface ($2B + D = 144\text{ kbps}$) and Primary Rate Interface ($30B + D = 2.048\text{ Mbps}$) architectures, reference points ($R, S, T, U$), and terminal equipment.
questions.solutionOutline: End-to-end digital telecommunication network for voice, data, video. Channel types: B-channel (64 kbps, bearer data), D-channel (16/64 kbps, signaling). BRI: 2B (64k) + 1D (16k) = 144 kbps over 2-wire copper pair. PRI: E1-based 30B (64k) + 1D (64k) = 2.048 Mbps. Reference points: U (2-wire line interface), T (separates user premises from network provider), S (separates terminal equipment from network termination), R (interface for non-ISDN devices using Terminal Adapter TA).

questions.text: Describe Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM). Explain the fixed 53-byte ATM cell structure (5-byte header, 48-byte payload), Virtual Path Identifier (VPI), Virtual Channel Identifier (VCI), and ATM Adaptation Layer (AAL) classes.
questions.solutionOutline: Fast packet-switching connection-oriented technology for B-ISDN. Fixed 53-byte cell ensures predictable low latency for voice/video. Header (5 bytes): GFC, VPI/VCI (hierarchical routing labels), Payload Type (PT), Cell Loss Priority (CLP), Header Error Control (HEC). AAL classes: AAL1 (Constant Bit Rate - CBR voice/video), AAL2 (Variable Bit Rate - VBR audio), AAL3/4 (connection-oriented data), AAL5 (SEAL - simple efficient adaptation for IP over ATM).

questions.text: Explain Optical Access Networks: Fiber-to-the-Home (FTTH) and Passive Optical Networks (PON). Compare Gigabit PON (GPON) and Ethernet PON (EPON) architectures, optical splitters, Optical Line Terminal (OLT), and Optical Network Unit (ONU/ONT).
questions.solutionOutline: PON connects central office to multiple subscriber premises using passive unpowered optical splitters (1:32 or 1:64) eliminating active field electronics. OLT at central office broadcasts downstream at 1490 nm using TDM; ONUs transmit upstream at 1310 nm using TDMA with dynamic bandwidth allocation (DBA). GPON provides 2.488 Gbps downstream / 1.244 Gbps upstream using GEM encapsulation. EPON provides 1.25 Gbps symmetrical native Ethernet frames.

questions.text: Explain Multi-Protocol Label Switching (MPLS). Describe Label Switched Routers (LSR), Label Edge Routers (LER), Label Distribution Protocol (LDP), and how MPLS enables Traffic Engineering and Layer-3 VPNs.
questions.solutionOutline: MPLS directs data using 32-bit short path labels between Layer 2 and Layer 3 (shim header: 20-bit label, 3-bit Exp/QoS, 1-bit Bottom-of-Stack, 8-bit TTL). Ingress LER classifies packet into Forwarding Equivalence Class (FEC) and pushes label. Core LSRs swap labels at line rate without inspecting IP headers. Egress LER pops label and forwards IP packet. MPLS-TE overrides shortest path to balance link congestion; BGP/MPLS IP-VPN isolates enterprise routing tables using VRFs.

questions.text: Explain Next Generation Network (NGN) and IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS). Describe the architectural separation of transport layer, control layer (Softswitch/MGC), and application service layer with the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP).
questions.solutionOutline: NGN separates telecom infrastructure into 3 decoupled planes: Transport stratum (packet-switched IP/MPLS core), Control stratum (Softswitch / Media Gateway Controller MGC managing call sessions via Megaco/H.248), and Application stratum (SIP application servers providing voice, video, IPTV). IMS provides standardized 3GPP SIP-based session control (P-CSCF, I-CSCF, S-CSCF, HSS) enabling seamless fixed-mobile convergence (FMC).
